clue.text: Presumably an all-round get-together for entertainment!

definitions.text: Presumably an all-round get-together for entertainment!

parts.words: Presumably an all-round get-together for entertainment
parts.note: a dance party is pictured as a party that is round all over, like a sphere

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that a party where everyone mixes is the sort thrown for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All-round' looks like 'involving everyone', but it plays on the dance's other sense, a spherical object.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal dance gathering shares its name with the round plaything, hence the pun.

clue.text: Stands about, as it were-for the finest trips?

parts.note: the finest means the best
trips or journeys on horseback are rides

explanation.surface: Someone loiters around, wondering which outings are the best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' is a link word joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand with legs either side of something is to straddle it, a stance loosely described as standing about it.

clue.text: Courtly persons remaining in expectation?

parts.note: attendants at a royal court are read literally as women who stay on, waiting for something

explanation.surface: Members of a royal household wait hopefully for something to happen.
explanation.definitionFit: A queen's female attendants hold this title, read here literally as women who are waiting.

clue.text: Tradesman can make break

indicators.note: the letters of the next word can be made into another word by rearranging them

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper is able to cause a breakage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can make' signals that BREAK is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who bakes and sells bread is a classic small tradesman.

clue.text: A pair lets ornaments appear

parts.note: a brace is a pair, as of game birds
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two of something allow decorations to come into view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appear' is a link word; a BRACE is a pair, as in a brace of pheasants.
explanation.definitionFit: Bands worn around the wrist are decorative jewellery, a kind of ornament.

clue.text: The lowest ships' stabilisers!

parts.note: the clue describes the timber spine running along the very bottom of a vessel, which keeps it steady

explanation.surface: The poorest vessels' steadying devices are mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The lowest' seems to rank the ships, but it describes where the structure sits: at the bottom of the hull.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel's backbone runs along the bottom of the hull and keeps it upright in the water.

clue.text: Old imperialist type

definitions.meaning: a citizen of the ancient empire based in Italy
the upright typeface used in ordinary printing

explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of the ancient Italian empire, and also the plain upright style of printing letters.

clue.text: Silly fellows used to drink

definitions.meaning: gullible people, easy dupes
cups with handles that people drink from

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for gullible dupes, and also large handled cups for tea or beer.

clue.text: We hear, Len's things seem bigger through this

definitions.text: We hear, Len's things seem bigger through this

parts.words: We hear, Len's things seem bigger through this
parts.note: the name Len with a possessive sounds like the optical word for a piece of curved glass, and through one things look larger

explanation.surface: Apparently, a man named Len's possessions look larger when viewed this way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Len's' sounds like 'lens', the curved glass at the heart of the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A handheld lens enlarges what is seen through it, the reading aid of detectives.

clue.text: Old dandy is to expand

definitions.meaning: an old-fashioned word for a fashionable gentleman
to grow larger, as a wave or a bruise does

explanation.definitionFit: Dated slang for a fashionable gentleman, and also a verb meaning to grow bigger.

clue.text: A comestible we might expect to grow, if planted?

definitions.text: A comestible we might expect to grow, if planted?

parts.words: A comestible we might expect to grow, if planted
parts.note: a baked treat named after what gardeners sow is imagined sprouting if put in the soil

explanation.surface: Some food that would sprout if buried in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The cake contains caraway, and its name suggests something you would sow.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional cake flavoured with caraway is named for what it contains.

clue.text: A pig-me? Wrong, a bird

indicators.note: the letters are set out in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they are a pygmy and is told no, they are a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong' signals that A, P, I, G, M, E are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The black-and-white thieving corvid is a familiar bird.

clue.text: Five hundred in Greece, not starting to turn and go back

indicators.note: the letters are made to turn about into a new order

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

indicators.note: the word is used without its starting letter

explanation.surface: Five hundred people in Greece, minus a beginner, turn round and retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not starting' removes the G of GREECE to leave REECE; 'to turn' rearranges D plus REECE. 'In' and 'and' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw or move away, as a tide does, is to retreat.

clue.text: Despatched drunken Nile guard

parts.note: despatched means sent off

indicators.note: drunken suggests the letters are staggering about out of order

explanation.surface: An inebriated soldier on the Nile is sent home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunken' looks like it describes a guard, but it is the anagram signal acting on the river's name alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier posted to keep watch is a lookout or sentry.

clue.text: Oddly, some microscopic creatures do it to multiply

definitions.text: Oddly, some microscopic creatures do it to multiply

parts.words: Oddly, some microscopic creatures do it to multiply
parts.note: the paradox is that single-celled organisms increase their numbers by splitting in two, the arithmetic opposite of multiplying

explanation.surface: Strangely, tiny organisms increase their numbers this way.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on arithmetic: the opposite operation to multiplying is how bacteria breed.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacteria reproduce by splitting, the arithmetic opposite of multiplying.

clue.text: Ground under if travelling like this!

definitions.text: Ground under if travelling like this!

parts.words: Ground under if travelling like this
parts.note: travelling through the air leaves the earth below you

explanation.surface: A traveller notes the land beneath them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like an anagram signal, but no rearrangement is meant; the land is literally below an air traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling by air keeps the earth far beneath, as in an aeroplane journey.

clue.text: Physical capabilities for describing university departments?

definitions.meaning: powers of the body or mind, such as sight and hearing
divisions of a university, such as law or arts

explanation.walkthrough: 'For describing' is a link joining the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Powers such as hearing or reason, and also the academic divisions of a university.

clue.text: Country for men about town, might one say?

definitions.text: Country for men about town, might one say?

parts.words: Country for men about town, might one say
parts.note: a man about town is a fashionable socialite, but read literally the phrase describes open land lying around a town

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what kind of rural place suits fashionable urban gentlemen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men about town' suggests socialites; read literally it is open country ringing a town. In Britain the protected countryside around a city has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Protected open countryside encircling a city where building is restricted.

clue.text: First, some come out with lowering sneers and angry looks

indicators.note: the first letters of the following six words are taken in turn

explanation.surface: Some people emerge with glowering contempt and furious stares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' takes the initial letters of 'some come out with lowering sneers'. 'And' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Frowns of displeasure are angry facial expressions.

clue.text: Monarch who attempted our main alteration, it's said!

definitions.text: Monarch who attempted our main alteration, it's said!

parts.words: Monarch who attempted our main alteration, it's said
parts.note: legend tells of a king who tried to change the sea (the main) by ordering the tide back

explanation.surface: A ruler who, the story goes, tried to change the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is an old word for the sea; 'it's said' marks this as legend, not a homophone. The 11th-century king of England, Denmark and Norway reputedly ordered the tide to retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danish-born king of England is remembered for the tale of commanding the waves.

clue.text: Monastic place-it finally recoils and goes wrong

indicators.note: the letters go wrong, ending up in a new order
finally takes the closing letter of the word it

explanation.surface: In a monastery, something springs back and malfunctions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' gives T from 'it'; 'goes wrong' rearranges T plus RECOILS.
explanation.definitionFit: A covered walkway round a monastery quadrangle, standing for monastic seclusion.

clue.text: Blows on one's wrists

definitions.meaning: light hits with the open hand
the ends of shirt sleeves at the wrist

explanation.definitionFit: Light slaps, and also the bands at the end of shirt sleeves.

clue.text: Mean a tippler often is? Yes!

definitions.meaning: stingy with money
a heavy drinker is frequently drunk

explanation.walkthrough: 'Yes!' only adds emphasis.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang both for stingy with money and for drunk, as a heavy drinker often is.

clue.text: Laughs a lot like a big cat?

definitions.meaning: guffaws loudly
makes the deep cry of a lion

explanation.definitionFit: Bellows of laughter, and also the deep growl a lion makes.

clue.text: Both the British and the foreign one famed for many old soldiers

definitions.text: Both the British and the foreign one famed for many old soldiers

parts.words: Both the British and the foreign one famed for many old soldiers
parts.note: the clue points to the veterans' charity in Britain and the French force of overseas recruits, both sharing one name meaning a host

explanation.surface: Two famous bodies, one British and one foreign, both known for their veterans.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal British Legion is a UK veterans' charity; the Foreign Legion is France's corps of overseas volunteers. The word also means a great number, as of a Roman army unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman army division, and by extension a multitude; also the name of two famous military bodies.

clue.text: Rubbing down furniture in the office for it!

definitions.meaning: smoothing with an abrasive tool

definitions.text: furniture in the office for it
definitions.meaning: the office cabinet used for storing papers in order

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense hints at the filing cabinet: the activity that office furniture is for.
explanation.definitionFit: Smoothing with a rasp, and also storing documents in a cabinet.

clue.text: Friendly French friend gets a telegram

parts.note: ami is French for friend
a cable is an old word for a telegram sent overseas

explanation.surface: A pleasant Frenchman receives a wire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets a' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on good terms and well disposed toward someone, as in a peaceable divorce.

clue.text: Garden pest may rush from the barrel

definitions.meaning: a slimy shell-less mollusc that eats plants
a bullet fired from a gun barrel, or a gulp of liquor from a cask

explanation.definitionFit: A shell-less mollusc that eats plants, and also a bullet or a swig of spirits.

clue.text: Jobs for the Russian agency concealing a letter

indicators.note: concealing means one piece hides another inside it

parts.note: TASS is the Russian news agency
K is one letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Work assignments from a Moscow news bureau that is hiding a message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A letter' looks like a message, but it is a single letter of the alphabet, here K.
explanation.definitionFit: Pieces of work to be done are duties or assignments.

clue.text: It's a place to see!

definitions.meaning: a particular location
to catch sight of or notice

explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A particular location, and also a verb meaning to catch sight of.
